district.description: Situated on the banks of the Amaravathi river, Karur was the ancient capital of the early Chera kings of the Sangam era. Today, it is a major hub for home textile exports.

culturalEntries.title: Kalyana Pasupatheeswarar Temple
culturalEntries.shortDescription: An ancient Shiva temple associated with the Chera dynasty and sung about by the Nayanmar poet-saints in the Tevaram.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Considered the first of the seven sacred Shivalayams of the Kongu region (Kongu Nadu), the Kalyana Pasupatheeswarar Temple boasts a history deeply intertwined with the Sangam-era Chera kings. The presiding deity is a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Lingam slightly tilted to one side. According to legend, the divine cow Kamadhenu worshipped Shiva here, giving the deity the name 'Pasupatheeswarar' (Lord of the Cow). It features a grand 5-tiered Rajagopuram and a unique 100-pillared hall.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Believed to be established during the early Chera period; extensive structure developed by later Cholas and Pandyas.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A vital Paadal Petra Sthalam (temple sung in the Tevaram). The temple serves as the spiritual heart of the ancient Kongu Nadu region and stands as a testament to Chera era religious patronage.
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: State Archaeological and Historical Documentation; Tamil Nadu Tourism

chatbotKnowledge.answerEn: The Kalyana Pasupatheeswarar Temple in Karur was deeply associated with the ancient Chera kings. Legend states that the divine cow Kamadhenu worshipped Lord Shiva here, and it is a prominent temple in the Kongu Nadu region.
chatbotKnowledge.answerTa: கரூரில் உள்ள கல்யாண பசுபதீஸ்வரர் கோயில், சேர மன்னர்களுடன் தொடர்புடைய பழமையான சிவன்கோயில் ஆகும். காமதேனு இங்கு சிவனை வழிபட்டதாகப் புராணங்கள் கூறுகின்றன. இது கொங்கு நாட்டின் மிக முக்கியமான திருத்தலமாகும்.
